en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn to tell a good story in English: what was happening, what happened, and how it ended. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: The shape of a story
steps.text: Everyone has stories: a funny moment, a scary night, a trip, a problem at work. Let's give yours a clear shape.
steps.body:
A good story has **three parts**:
1. **Set the scene**: when, where, who, and what was happening.
2. **What happened**: the events, one after another.
3. **How it ended** and **how you felt**.
Start with a time (*Last Lebaran…, Yesterday…, A few years ago…*) so your listener knows it's a past story. Keep the scene short (one or two sentences), then move to the action.

steps.title: Words that move the story
steps.text: You know first, then and after that. Stories need three more.
steps.body: **suddenly** (*tiba-tiba*) = something quick that nobody expected. **in the end** (*akhirnya*) = the final result, after problems or changes. **at the end of** + a noun = *di akhir*: *at the end of the film*. Not *in the end of* ✗. **finally** = the last event, or the end of a long wait (*Finally, the bus came*). Careful: when *akhirnya* means a **result**, use **so** (*It rained, so we stayed home*).

pairs.en: at the end of the month

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Sari tells you about her mudik. The parts are mixed up.

question.prompt:
Put Sari's mudik story in order.
A: In the end, we got to Grandma's house just before midnight.
B: It was the day before Lebaran, and the roads were full of cars.
C: Suddenly our car broke down on the toll road.
question.explanation: **B** sets the scene (when, and what the roads were like). **C** is what happened: **Suddenly** brings a quick, unexpected event. **A** is the ending: **In the end** = the final result after the problem.

steps.title: Three tenses, one story
steps.text: You know all three past tenses. In a story, each has a job.
steps.body:
**was/were + -ing** = the **background**, what was already happening: *It was raining.*
**past simple** = the **events**, in order: *The bus came. I got on.*
**had + third form** = going **back** to something **earlier**: *I had forgotten my umbrella.*
**Indonesian trap:** Indonesian verbs don't change (*Kemarin saya pergi … dan saya lihat …*), so learners say *Yesterday I go … and I see …* ✗. In English **every** verb in a past story changes: *I **went** … and I **saw** …* ✓.

steps.title: A morning on the KRL
steps.text: Here's a short story with all three tenses. Look at what each verb does.
steps.body: Scene → **was/were + -ing** (*was standing, were looking*). Events → **past simple** (*stopped, got*). Going back → **had** + third form (*had died* = the battery died before that).

examples.en: It was Monday morning, and the KRL to Jakarta was packed.
examples.id: Senin pagi itu, KRL ke Jakarta penuh sesak.

examples.en: I was standing near the door, and everyone was looking at their phones.
examples.id: Aku sedang berdiri dekat pintu, dan semua orang sedang melihat HP mereka.

examples.en: Suddenly the train stopped between two stations.
examples.id: Tiba-tiba keretanya berhenti di antara dua stasiun.

examples.en: I wanted to call my boss, but my phone had died.
examples.id: Aku mau menelepon bosku, tapi HP-ku sudah mati (baterainya habis).

examples.en: In the end, I got to the office forty minutes late. Luckily, my boss was late too!
examples.id: Akhirnya, aku sampai di kantor terlambat empat puluh menit. Untungnya, bosku juga terlambat!

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Now a bad start to a work day.

question.prompt: Complete: When I got to the office, I realised I ___ my laptop at home.
question.explanation: Getting to the office and realising are the story events (past simple). Leaving the laptop happened **earlier**, so go back with had + third form: **had left**. 'leave' is the Indonesian no-tense trap, and 'was leaving' means you were in the middle of leaving.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: A wedding dinner, and then a surprise. Put the long action after While.

question.prompt: Arrange the words. Start with While: Saat kami sedang makan, lampunya mati.
question.explanation: The eating is the background (**were eating**, after **while**); the lights going out is the short event (past simple: **went out**). The while part comes first, so a comma follows it.
question.solution: While we were eating, the lights went out.

steps.title: Details, feelings and reactions
steps.text: A list of events is boring. Bring your story to life, and react to other people's stories.
steps.body: Add **details** (who, where, what you saw) and **feelings**: *I couldn't believe it!* (aku nggak percaya!) *It was so embarrassing!* **Luckily, …** (untungnya) before good news, **Unfortunately, …** (sayangnya) before bad news. **-ing** = the situation (*embarrassing* = memalukan); **-ed** = how a person feels (*embarrassed* = malu). *I was so embarrassing* ✗. When you **listen**, react with the phrases below, and match the mood.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas tells you about his birthday.

question.prompt: Complete Dimas's story: When I opened the door, all my friends shouted 'Happy birthday!' I was so ___.
question.explanation: This is how Dimas **felt**, so use the **-ed** word: **surprised** (kaget). **surprising** describes the situation (*The news was surprising*), and **surprise** is a noun.

steps.title: Listen and react
steps.text: Your friend starts a story. Press play and listen.

question.prompt: Listen to your friend's story. Choose the most natural reaction.
question.explanation: Your friend stopped at the exciting part, so show surprise and ask for more: **Really? What happened next?** 'Lucky you!' is for good news, and 'Yes, I was' doesn't answer anything.
question.listen: I was riding an ojek to the office this morning. Suddenly the driver stopped in the middle of a busy road, turned around and looked at me.
options: Yes, I was. How about you?

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for your next story.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · telling stories
artifact.intro: Scene → what happened → how it ended and how you felt. Every verb in a past story is in a past form.
rows: It was raining, and everyone was waiting.
The train came, and we got on.
After that, we took an ojek.
In the end, we got home at midnight.
at the end of the film
It was so embarrassing. I was so embarrassed.
tips: Every verb in a past story changes: 'Yesterday I go … and I see …' ✗ → **Yesterday I went … and I saw …** ✓.
**At the end of** + a noun (*at the end of the film*); **in the end** alone = the final result. Not *in the end of*.
Match your reaction to the mood: **Oh no!** for bad news, **No way!** for surprise, **What happened next?** to hear more.

examples.en: It was the day before Lebaran, and we were driving to Solo.
examples.id: Waktu itu sehari sebelum Lebaran, dan kami sedang menyetir ke Solo.

examples.en: Suddenly our car made a strange noise and stopped.
examples.id: Tiba-tiba mobil kami mengeluarkan suara aneh lalu berhenti.

examples.en: We couldn't call anyone because our phones had died.
examples.id: Kami tidak bisa menelepon siapa pun karena HP kami sudah mati.

examples.en: Luckily, a mechanic came and fixed the car.
examples.id: Untungnya, seorang montir datang dan memperbaiki mobilnya.

examples.en: In the end, we got to my grandmother's house at midnight. I couldn't believe it!
examples.id: Akhirnya, kami sampai di rumah nenek tengah malam. Aku nggak percaya!

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more? Here's a video lesson, all in English, on building a story step by step.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu belajar bercerita dengan baik dalam bahasa Inggris: apa yang sedang terjadi, apa yang terjadi, dan bagaimana akhirnya. Ayo kita pelajari pelan-pelan.

steps.title: Bentuk sebuah cerita
steps.text: Semua orang punya cerita: momen lucu, malam yang menyeramkan, perjalanan, masalah di kantor. Yuk beri ceritamu bentuk yang jelas.
steps.body:
Cerita yang bagus punya **tiga bagian**:
1. **Bangun latarnya**: kapan, di mana, siapa, dan apa yang sedang terjadi.
2. **Apa yang terjadi**: kejadian-kejadiannya, satu per satu.
3. **Bagaimana akhirnya** dan **apa yang kamu rasakan**.
Mulai dengan keterangan waktu (*Last Lebaran…, Yesterday…, A few years ago…*) supaya pendengarmu tahu ini cerita masa lalu. Buat latarnya singkat (satu atau dua kalimat), lalu masuk ke kejadiannya.

steps.title: Kata-kata yang menggerakkan cerita
steps.text: Kamu sudah tahu first, then dan after that. Cerita butuh tiga lagi.
steps.body: **suddenly** (*tiba-tiba*) = sesuatu yang cepat dan tidak ada yang menduga. **in the end** (*akhirnya*) = hasil akhirnya, setelah ada masalah atau perubahan. **at the end of** + kata benda = *di akhir*: *at the end of the film*. Bukan *in the end of* ✗. **finally** = kejadian terakhir, atau akhir dari penantian panjang (*Finally, the bus came*). Hati-hati: kalau *akhirnya* berarti **akibat**, pakai **so** (*It rained, so we stayed home*).

pairs.en: at the end of the month

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sari bercerita tentang mudiknya. Bagian-bagiannya tercampur.

question.prompt:
Urutkan cerita mudik Sari.
A: In the end, we got to Grandma's house just before midnight.
B: It was the day before Lebaran, and the roads were full of cars.
C: Suddenly our car broke down on the toll road.
question.explanation: **B** membangun latar (kapan, dan seperti apa jalanannya). **C** adalah apa yang terjadi: **Suddenly** membawa kejadian yang cepat dan tidak terduga. **A** adalah akhirnya: **In the end** = hasil akhir setelah masalahnya.

steps.title: Tiga tense, satu cerita
steps.text: Kamu sudah tahu ketiga past tense. Dalam cerita, masing-masing punya tugas.
steps.body:
**was/were + -ing** = **latar**, apa yang sedang terjadi: *It was raining.*
**past simple** = **kejadian-kejadiannya**, berurutan: *The bus came. I got on.*
**had + bentuk ketiga** = **kembali** ke sesuatu yang terjadi **lebih dulu**: *I had forgotten my umbrella.*
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** kata kerja kita tidak berubah (*Kemarin saya pergi … dan saya lihat …*), jadi banyak yang bilang *Yesterday I go … and I see …* ✗. Dalam bahasa Inggris **setiap** kata kerja dalam cerita lampau berubah: *I **went** … and I **saw** …* ✓.

steps.title: Pagi hari di KRL
steps.text: Ini cerita pendek dengan ketiga tense. Perhatikan tugas setiap kata kerjanya.
steps.body: Latar → **was/were + -ing** (*was standing, were looking*). Kejadian → **past simple** (*stopped, got*). Kembali ke masa sebelumnya → **had** + bentuk ketiga (*had died* = baterainya habis sebelum itu).

examples.id: Senin pagi itu, KRL ke Jakarta penuh sesak.

examples.en: I was standing near the door, and everyone was looking at their phones.
examples.id: Aku sedang berdiri dekat pintu, dan semua orang sedang melihat HP mereka.

examples.en: Suddenly the train stopped between two stations.
examples.id: Tiba-tiba keretanya berhenti di antara dua stasiun.

examples.en: I wanted to call my boss, but my phone had died.
examples.id: Aku mau menelepon bosku, tapi HP-ku sudah mati (baterainya habis).

examples.en: In the end, I got to the office forty minutes late. Luckily, my boss was late too!

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sekarang awal hari kerja yang buruk.

question.prompt: Lengkapi (realise = sadar): When I got to the office, I realised I ___ my laptop at home.
question.explanation: Sampai di kantor dan menyadari adalah kejadian dalam cerita (past simple). Laptopnya ketinggalan **lebih dulu**, jadi kembali ke masa itu dengan had + bentuk ketiga: **had left**. 'leave' adalah jebakan tanpa tense dari bahasa Indonesia, dan 'was leaving' berarti kamu sedang dalam proses pergi.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Makan malam di pesta nikahan, lalu kejutan. Taruh kegiatan panjangnya setelah While.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya. Mulai dengan While: Saat kami sedang makan, lampunya mati.
question.explanation: Makan adalah latarnya (**were eating**, setelah **while**); lampu mati adalah kejadian singkatnya (past simple: **went out**). Bagian while ada di depan, jadi diikuti koma.
question.solution: While we were eating, the lights went out.

steps.title: Detail, perasaan dan reaksi
steps.text: Daftar kejadian saja itu membosankan. Hidupkan ceritamu, dan beri reaksi pada cerita orang lain.
steps.body: Tambahkan **detail** (siapa, di mana, apa yang kamu lihat) dan **perasaan**: *I couldn't believe it!* (aku nggak percaya!) *It was so embarrassing!* (malu banget!) **Luckily, …** (untungnya) sebelum kabar baik, **Unfortunately, …** (sayangnya) sebelum kabar buruk. **-ing** = situasinya (*embarrassing* = memalukan); **-ed** = perasaan seseorang (*embarrassed* = malu). *I was so embarrassing* ✗. Saat **mendengarkan**, beri reaksi dengan ungkapan di bawah, sesuai suasana ceritanya.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dimas bercerita tentang ulang tahunnya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi cerita Dimas: When I opened the door, all my friends shouted 'Happy birthday!' I was so ___.
question.explanation: Ini tentang **perasaan** Dimas, jadi pakai kata **-ed**: **surprised** (kaget). **surprising** menggambarkan situasinya (*The news was surprising*), dan **surprise** adalah kata benda.

steps.title: Dengarkan dan beri reaksi
steps.text: Temanmu mulai bercerita. Tekan play dan dengarkan.

question.prompt: Dengarkan cerita temanmu. Pilih reaksi yang paling wajar.
question.explanation: Temanmu berhenti di bagian yang seru, jadi tunjukkan rasa kaget dan minta lanjutannya: **Really? What happened next?** 'Lucky you!' untuk kabar baik, dan 'Yes, I was' tidak menjawab apa pun.
question.listen: I was riding an ojek to the office this morning. Suddenly the driver stopped in the middle of a busy road, turned around and looked at me.
options: Yes, I was. How about you?

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk ceritamu berikutnya.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · bercerita
artifact.intro: Latar → apa yang terjadi → bagaimana akhirnya dan apa yang kamu rasakan. Setiap kata kerja dalam cerita lampau memakai bentuk lampau.
rows: It was raining, and everyone was waiting.
The train came, and we got on.
kembali ke sesuatu yang lebih dulu
After that, we took an ojek.
In the end, we got home at midnight.
at the end of the film
It was so embarrassing. I was so embarrassed.
tips: Setiap kata kerja dalam cerita lampau berubah: 'Yesterday I go … and I see …' ✗ → **Yesterday I went … and I saw …** ✓.
**At the end of** + kata benda (*at the end of the film*); **in the end** saja = hasil akhirnya. Bukan *in the end of*.
Sesuaikan reaksimu dengan suasananya: **Oh no!** untuk kabar buruk, **No way!** untuk kaget, **What happened next?** untuk minta lanjutannya.
